subtype: Approach: task decomposition with a shared board [Action]
passage:
Subject: Project plan, first update

Dear Irfan Sir,

Our team of four met on Saturday and cut the project into four parts: data collection, the model, the interface and the report. Each part became a set of small cards on one online board, and every card carries a name and a date. I took the interface, Meena took the data, and the other two took the model and the report. We agreed to look at the board together for ten minutes every Tuesday and Friday. After two weeks, nine of fourteen cards have moved to done, and two late cards were noticed early. Could we show you the board on Friday?

Regards,
Nazia

qa.q: How many cards had moved to done after two weeks?
qa.a: Nine of fourteen cards have moved to done.

qa.q: What is Nazia feeling as the update is written?
qa.a: Nazia seems proud and hopeful: the progress is reported with numbers, and asking to show the board suggests confidence.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the team use if cards keep slipping, and why?
qa.a: They could hold a short root-cause talk about the slipping cards, because a board shows what is late but not why it is late.

qa.q: How might Irfan Sir see this update?
qa.a: Irfan Sir gets a clear picture of who is doing what and when, so he can judge progress quickly and offer help early.

grounding: Shows a team breaking a project into parts, giving each card an owner and a date, and checking progress briefly twice weekly.
